intro: Plumbing helpers learn pipe systems, tools and job site routines. The closest of the 25 careers below is maintenance and repair helping at an 84% match, while Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters are 82% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $63,800, which is 51% more than helpers earn.
why_it_works: As a helper you cut and carry pipe, prepare work areas and watch licensed plumbers solve problems on every job. O*NET rates judgment at 2.88 out of 5 for this job and coordination at 2.75. Plumbing, pipelaying and carpentry build directly on that base. 24 of the 25 matches pay more than the $42,360 helper median. The gaps are quality checks and operating equipment.
tips: Ask about a plumbing apprenticeship; helpers often move into one with the same employer.
Boilermakers earn $76,410, which is 80% more, and use your pipe and welding exposure.
Pipelayers earn $49,000, or 16% more, with no extra training.

faq.q: What jobs can former plumbing helpers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are maintenance and repair helpers (84%), Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters (82%) and Pipelayers (82%), based on O*NET 31.0. Carpenters are 81% matched and earn $60,580, which is 43% more than the $42,360 median for plumbing helpers.

faq.q: Which careers for plumbing helpers pay more?
faq.a: 24 of the 25 matches pay more. Boilermakers earn $76,410 (80% more), Terrazzo Workers and Finishers $76,170 (80% more) and plumbers and pipefitters $63,800 (51% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Plumbing usually needs a certificate or apprenticeship and a license.

faq.q: Do plumbing helpers need more education to switch?
faq.a: Rarely. 24 of the 25 matches need no more education than plumbing helpers already have, including 9 of the top 10. A post-secondary certificate is common in close matches, held by 43% of workers in one, and apprenticeships pay while you learn.

faq.q: What skills should plumbing helpers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operations monitoring, quality control analysis, operation and control and equipment maintenance. Repairing already rates 2.62 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so taking on full repairs yourself is the main step toward a licensed trade.
